title: Migrating to Cache Components
nav_title: Migrating to Cache Components
description: Learn how to migrate from route segment configs to Cache Components in Next.js.
related:
  title: Next Steps
  description: Learn about other behavior changes when Cache Components is enabled.
  links:
    - app/guides/optimizing-the-static-shell
    - app/guides/instant-navigation
    - app/guides/preserving-ui-state
    - app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components
    - app/getting-started/caching
---

When [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled, route segment configs like `dynamic`, `revalidate`, and `fetchCache` are replaced by [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) and [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife).

The migration is driven by **instant navigation validation**. With Cache Components enabled, Next.js validates in development whether navigating into each route renders instantly, and surfaces the code that would block it as an error or insight.

## Use the adoption skill (recommended)

---
title: Migrating to Cache Components
nav_title: Migrating to Cache Components
description: Learn how to migrate from route segment configs to Cache Components in Next.js.
related:
  title: Next Steps
  description: Learn about other behavior changes when Cache Components is enabled.
  links:
    - app/guides/optimizing-the-static-shell
    - app/guides/instant-navigation
    - app/guides/preserving-ui-state
    - app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components
    - app/getting-started/caching
---

When [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled, route segment configs like `dynamic`, `revalidate`, and `fetchCache` are replaced by [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) and [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife).

The migration is driven by **instant navigation validation**. With Cache Components enabled, Next.js validates in development whether navigating into each route renders instantly, and surfaces the code that would block it as an error or insight.

## Use the adoption skill (recommended)

00003| description: Learn how to use the "use cache" directive to cache data in your Next.js application.
00004| related:

00014|     - app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag
00015| ---
00016| 
00017| The `use cache` directive allows you to mark a route, React component, or a function as cacheable. It can be used at the top of a file to indicate that all exports in the file should be cached, or inline at the top of a function or component to cache the return value. Functions and components that use `use cache` must be async.
00018| 
00019| > **Good to know:**
00020| >
00021| > - To use cookies or headers, read them outside cached scopes and pass values as arguments. This is the preferred pattern.
00022| > - If the in-memory cache isn't sufficient for runtime data, [`'use cache: remote'`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote) allows platforms to provide a dedicated cache handler, though it requires a network roundtrip to check the cache and typically incurs platform fees.
00023| > - For compliance requirements or when you can't refactor to pass runtime data as arguments to a `use cache` scope, see [`'use cache: private'`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private).
00024| 
00025| ## Usage
00026| 
00027| `use cache` is a Cache Components feature. To enable it, add the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) option to your `next.config.ts` file:
00028| 
00029| ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher
00030| import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
00031| 
00032| const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
00033|   cacheComponents: true,
00034| }
00035| 
00036| export default nextConfig
00037| ```
00038| 
00039| ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher
00040| /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
00041| const nextConfig = {
00042|   cacheComponents: true,
00043| }
00044| 
00045| module.exports = nextConfig
00046| ```
00047| 
00048| Then, add `use cache` at the function, component, or file level. Cached functions and components must be async:
00049| 
00050| ```tsx
00051| // Function level
00052| export async function getData() {
00053|   'use cache'
00054|   const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data')
00055|   const data = await res.json()
00056|   return data
00057| }
00058| 
00059| // Component level
00060| export async function MyComponent() {
00061|   'use cache'
00062|   return <></>
00063| }
00064| ```
00065| 
00066| When used at file level, every exported function becomes a cached function and must also be async:
00067| 
00068| ```tsx
00069| // File level
00070| 'use cache'
00071| 
00072| export default async function Page() {
00073|   // ...
00074| }
00075| ```
00076| 
00077| ## How `use cache` works
00078| 
00079| ### Cache keys
00080| 
00081| A cache entry's key is generated using a serialized version of its inputs, which includes:
00082| 
00083| 1. **Build ID** - Unique per build, changing this invalidates all cache entries. If [`deploymentId`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/deploymentId) is configured, it overrides the build ID for cache key purposes.
00084| 2. **Function ID** - A secure hash of the function's location and signature in the codebase
00085| 3. **Serializable arguments** - Props (for components) or function arguments
00086| 4. **HMR refresh hash** (development only) - Invalidates cache on hot module replacement
00087| 
00088| When a cached function references variables from outer scopes, those variables are automatically captured and bound as arguments, making them part of the cache key.
00089| 
00090| ```tsx filename="lib/data.ts"
00091| async function Component({ userId }: { userId: string }) {
00092|   const getData = async (filter: string) => {
00093|     'use cache'
00094|     // Cache key includes both userId (from closure) and filter (argument)
00095|     const res = await fetch(
00096|       `https://api.example.com/users/${userId}/data?filter=${filter}`
00097|     )
00098|     return res.json()
00099|   }
00100| 
00101|   return getData('active')
00102| }
00103| ```
00104| 
00105| In the snippet above, `userId` is captured from the outer scope and `filter` is passed as an argument, so both become part of the `getData` function's cache key. This means different user and filter combinations will have separate cache entries.
00106| 
00107| > **Good to know:** When a cached function reads [root parameters](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-root-params), only the ones it actually reads become part of its cache key.
00108| 
00109| ### Cache output
00110| 
00111| A cached function produces the same output for the same inputs. The first call with a given set of inputs runs the function body and stores its output. Every later call with the same inputs reuses that output, within a render pass and across requests, for as long as the entry lasts.
00112| 
00113| Outputs are stored by a [cache handler](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheHandlers), [in memory](#runtime-caching-considerations) by default, and last until they [revalidate](#revalidation).
00114| 
00115| ```tsx filename="lib/orders.ts"
00116| import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache'
00117| 
00118| export async function getOrderSummary(accountId: string) {
00119|   'use cache'
00120|   cacheLife('hours')
00121| 
00122|   const orders = await getOrders(accountId)
00123|   const totals = await getOrderTotals(accountId)
00124| 
00125|   return { orders, totals }
00126| }
00127| 
00128| export async function getOrders(accountId: string) {
00129|   'use cache'
00130|   cacheLife('hours')
00131| 
00132|   return db.orders.findMany({ where: { accountId } })
00133| }
00134| 
00135| export async function getOrderTotals(accountId: string) {
00136|   return db.orders.aggregate({ where: { accountId }, _sum: { amount: true } })
00137| }
00138| ```
00139| 
00140| In the example above, each `accountId` has its own entry for `getOrderSummary`, holding the serialized `{ orders, totals }` object it returns. Calls to `getOrders` have their own entries, keyed by the same `accountId`. If an earlier call, through the summary or directly, already filled one, `db.orders.findMany` doesn't run and those orders become part of the summary's output. See [nested caching behavior](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#nested-caching-behavior) for how an inner lifetime affects the entry around it.
00141| 
00142| Note that `getOrderTotals` is not cached. It is exported so other parts of the application can read fresh totals in an uncached scope. Inside `getOrderSummary`, though, the totals query only runs when that function runs following the `'hours'` lifetime set there.
00143| 
00144| With [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents), prerendering fills the entry and keeps rendering, so this output contributes to the route's [static shell](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#prerendering) and can contribute to its [prefetch](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#prefetching). A cache life too short to store safely leaves a hole that resolves at request time instead. See [prerendering behavior](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#prerendering-behavior) for the thresholds.
00145| 
00146| ## Serialization
00147| 
00148| Arguments to cached functions and their return values must be serializable.
00149|

00083| 1. **Build ID** - Unique per build, changing this invalidates all cache entries. If [`deploymentId`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/deploymentId) is configured, it overrides the build ID for cache key purposes.
00084| 2. **Function ID** - A secure hash of the function's location and signature in the codebase
00085| 3. **Serializable arguments** - Props (for components) or function arguments
00086| 4. **HMR refresh hash** (development only) - Invalidates cache on hot module replacement
00087| 
00088| When a cached function references variables from outer scopes, those variables are automatically captured and bound as arguments, making them part of the cache key.
00089| 
00090| ```tsx filename="lib/data.ts"
00091| async function Component({ userId }: { userId: string }) {
00092|   const getData = async (filter: string) => {
00093|     'use cache'
00094|     // Cache key includes both userId (from closure) and filter (argument)
00095|     const res = await fetch(
00096|       `https://api.example.com/users/${userId}/data?filter=${filter}`
00097|     )
00098|     return res.json()
00099|   }
00100| 
00101|   return getData('active')
00102| }
00103| ```
00104| 
00105| In the snippet above, `userId` is captured from the outer scope and `filter` is passed as an argument, so both become part of the `getData` function's cache key. This means different user and filter combinations will have separate cache entries.
00106| 
00107| > **Good to know:** When a cached function reads [root parameters](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-root-params), only the ones it actually reads become part of its cache key.
00108| 
00109| ### Cache output
00110| 
00111| A cached function produces the same output for the same inputs. The first call with a given set of inputs runs the function body and stores its output. Every later call with the same inputs reuses that output, within a render pass and across requests, for as long as the entry lasts.
00112| 
00113| Outputs are stored by a [cache handler](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheHandlers), [in memory](#runtime-caching-considerations) by default, and last until they [revalidate](#revalidation).
00114| 
00115| ```tsx filename="lib/orders.ts"
00116| import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache'
00117| 
00118| export async function getOrderSummary(accountId: string) {
00119|   'use cache'
00120|   cacheLife('hours')
00121| 
00122|   const orders = await getOrders(accountId)
00123|   const totals = await getOrderTotals(accountId)
00124| 
00125|   return { orders, totals }
00126| }
00127| 
00128| export async function getOrders(accountId: string) {
00129|   'use cache'
00130|   cacheLife('hours')
00131| 
00132|   return db.orders.findMany({ where: { accountId } })
00133| }
00134| 
00135| export async function getOrderTotals(accountId: string) {
00136|   return db.orders.aggregate({ where: { accountId }, _sum: { amount: true } })
00137| }
00138| ```
00139| 
00140| In the example above, each `accountId` has its own entry for `getOrderSummary`, holding the serialized `{ orders, totals }` object it returns. Calls to `getOrders` have their own entries, keyed by the same `accountId`. If an earlier call, through the summary or directly, already filled one, `db.orders.findMany` doesn't run and those orders become part of the summary's output. See [nested caching behavior](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#nested-caching-behavior) for how an inner lifetime affects the entry around it.
00141| 
00142| Note that `getOrderTotals` is not cached. It is exported so other parts of the application can read fresh totals in an uncached scope. Inside `getOrderSummary`, though, the totals query only runs when that function runs following the `'hours'` lifetime set there.
00143| 
00144| With [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents), prerendering fills the entry and keeps rendering, so this output contributes to the route's [static shell](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#prerendering) and can contribute to its [prefetch](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#prefetching). A cache life too short to store safely leaves a hole that resolves at request time instead. See [prerendering behavior](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#prerendering-behavior) for the thresholds.
00145| 
00146| ## Serialization
00147| 
00148| Arguments to cached functions and their return values must be serializable.
00149| 
00150| For a complete reference, see:
00151|

metadata.preview:
title: use cache
description: Learn how to use the "use cache" directive to cache data in your Next.js application.
related:
  title: Related
  description: View related API references.
  links:
    - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private
    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents
    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheLife
    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheHandlers
    - app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag
    - app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife
    - app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag
---

The `use cache` directive allows you to mark a route, React component, or a function as cacheable. It can be used at the top of a file to indicate that all exports in the file should be cached, or inline at the top of a function or component to cache the return value. Functions and components that use `use cache` must be async.

> **Good to know:**
>
> - To use cookies or headers, read them outside cached scopes and pass values as arguments. This is the preferred pattern.

events.content:
The application has been migrated to Cache Components and built for production:

- **`next.config.ts`**: Replaced `experimental.dynamicIO` with `cacheComponents: true`.
- **`app/news/page.tsx`**: Removed `export const revalidate = 3600` and applied `'use cache'` with `cacheLife('hours')`.
- **`app/preview/page.tsx`**: Removed `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` and moved the request-specific `cookies()` read into a `<Suspense>` boundary so the static shell prerenders while the draft preview streams per request.

The application has been migrated to Cache Components and built for production:

- **`next.config.ts`**: Replaced `experimental.dynamicIO` with `cacheComponents: true`.
- **`app/news/page.tsx`**: Removed `export const revalidate = 3600` and applied `'use cache'` with `cacheLife('hours')`.
- **`app/preview/page.tsx`**: Removed `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` and moved the request-specific `cookies()` read into a `<Suspense>` boundary so the static shell prerenders while the draft preview streams per request.
